object_description: four raised wings arranged around a central circulation ring
design_condition: Four buildings are raised above the flood level around a central ring, but their disconnection from the ground and schematic landscape integration weaken the relationship with the site.

positive.statement: The cells distributed along two facades offer a diversity of views and orientations.
The three wings housing the six divisions have a fairly clear organization.
The structural, technical-distribution, and sustainability responses are adequate.
The phasing is well designed, with small contact surfaces facilitating realization of the second phase.
The project author plans areas for later expansion.

negative.statement: The small patios raise questions about their real usefulness and compliance with regulations.
The great depth of the lower floors greatly reduces natural light in the workshops.
Raising the buildings solves flooding but leaves them disconnected from the ground, while the stairs and ramps are not integrated into the architecture.
The residual arrangement of buildings and promenades does not provide the privacy required for security.
The project does not convincingly integrate into the landscape, which remains very schematic.
The mix of functions in the central building raises questions about the establishment’s functioning.
Access from the distant divisions requires crossing other divisions, creating problematic circulation.
The high-security division is too exposed to contact with other prisoners and people outside the establishment.
Logistical circulation creates risks of contact between prisoners and external people across the site.
The great building depth creates problems for horizontal evacuation routes.
The second-degree evolution of the concept is unconvincing and introduces functionality issues that were previously absent.
The proposed expansion areas are not shown to work as a coherent whole.
